title: Thuringian states
capsule: The Thuringian Kingdom was a Germanic polity that emerged in the post-Hunnic power vacuum of central Germany in the early 5th century, comprising a confederation of tribes (the Thuringii) who occupied the territory between the Elbe, Saale, and Rhine rivers. During its period of independence it engaged in conflict with Saxons to the north and maintained an ambiguous relationship with the expanding Frankish kingdom to the west. The dataset's attestation window of 469–476 captures the kingdom at the moment of the Western Roman Empire's dissolution, a period in which Thuringia operated as one of several successor Germanic polities. The kingdom was definitively conquered by the Franks under Theodoric I and Chlothar I in 531, its ruling dynasty massacred, and its territory incorporated into the Frankish realm.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Thuringian Kingdom's territorial extent in this early period is poorly attested; boundaries are inferred from later Frankish administrative records and cannot be mapped with precision.
